title: partner-outreach-novus-bank-scratchpad
content:
Personal scratchpad — Novus Bank outreach

Purpose: quick account research + 1:many outbound drafts + objection response crib notes. Save for call prep and to spin into a tailored one-pager later.

Account high-level
- Company: Novus Bank (mid-sized regional bank, heavy retail + small business)
- HQ: Chicago; 22 branch locations in Midwest, large digital app user base (~1.2M MAU)
- Signals: recent press about migrating payments stack to new cloud provider (Nov 2025), job posts for "Platform Reliability" and "AI Payments" roles, regulatory filing mentioning vendor consolidation.
- Likely priorities: data residency & compliance, predictable economics (per-transaction), latency for customer-facing chatbots, auditability/tracing for model outputs.
- Potential objections: security/compliance, on-prem vs hosted, cost transparency, SLA guarantees, model hallucination risk in financial domain.

Key contacts (from LinkedIn / company web) — double-check emails before outreach\- Elena Myers — Head of Platform (engineer background)\- Priya Sethi — Director, Risk & Compliance\- Marcus Gruber — Product manager, Digital Banking
Notes: Elena occasionally posts about infra observability; Priya was previously at a payments compliance team (good sign for empathy on traceability).

Quick thesis for outreach (2 lines)\- "We help banks run LLM-powered features with predictable latency, explicit audit logs, and deployment options that meet strict compliance — hosted, VPC, or fully on-prem. I'd love to share a short checklist we use to map model risk to controls."

Cold email drafts (A/B test)
A — short, product-focused\Subject: Can Novus keep fraud chat latency <100ms while staying audit-ready?\Hi Elena — quick note: we helped a regional bank replace a brittle rules+ML fraud triage flow with a hybrid LLM pipeline that cut false-positive review time by 40% while preserving audit trails. If you have 15 minutes next week, I can share the checklist we used to map controls to deployment modes.\Thanks,\Jordan

B — personalized, compliance-first\Subject: Audit trails & model controls for customer chat at Novus\Priya — spotted your note on vendor consolidation. We built a small prescriptive framework for financial customers that ties prompt-level traceability to existing audit logs (KMS, HSM integration included). Short 20-min call = example mapping + cost/latency tradeoffs. Open to intro?\Jordan

LinkedIn outreach (short)\- "Hi Elena — I work with engineering teams at banks to make LLM features production-safe (low latency + auditable). Quick Q: do you prefer vendor-hosted endpoints or VPC/on-prem for production models?"\\(follow-up if no reply: share concrete stat e.g., "Banks we work with reduce per-interaction cost by 30% with caching+quantization")

Discovery checklist (what to learn in first call)
- Primary use cases? (chat, search, fraud triage, KYC automation)
- Current infra: cloud provider, are there VPC- or on-prem constraints?\- Regulatory constraints: data residency, retention period, audit log format\- Latency SLOs and P95 targets for each route\- Existing model stack (in-house vs vendor; model sizes)\- Failure modes they worry about (hallucination, leakage, availability)\- Decision criteria & timeline for vendor selection

Objection handling crib notes\- "We can't put customer data in a third-party cloud" -> Response: "Totally understood. We offer Private (VPC) deployments and an on-prem option; control plane can be self-hosted or tenant-isolated. We also integrate with customer KMS/HSM so keys never leave your boundary."\- "We need hard SLAs for latency and uptime" -> "Dedicated capacity gives reserved GPU pools and burst options with SLA-backed latency targets; we can run a short pilot with your key routes to baseline P95 and tune batching/cache."\- "Models hallucinate — we can't have that in banking" -> "We provide structured output enforcement, function/tool calling, and eval hooks tied to your prompt sets. Also can fall back to deterministic rule pipelines for high-risk flows."\- "Vendor lock-in / long contracts" -> "We expose model versioning and a consistent API so you can switch model backends. Dedicated capacity contracts are flexible and we also support an exit/republish migration plan."

Pilot proposal (30/60/90 sketch to propose later)\- Week 0–2: discovery + data access agreement + security review (Priya involvement)\- Week 2–4: small pilot deploy (sandbox VPC or hosted with strict logging) — one route (chat or fraud triage) instrumented for latency/cost/traceability metrics\- Week 4–8: tune batching, caching, and quantization profiles; integrate KMS; run adversarial evals with their prompts\- Week 8–12: production cutover plan, runbook, SLO definition, training for ops teams

Metrics to show in a deck/pilot results\- P95 latency (ms), tokens/sec, cost per 1k interactions, % false positives (if fraud), % of outputs with provenance metadata, audit log retention and retrieval time

Collateral to attach (notes to self)\- One-pager: "LLM controls for regulated financial apps" (draft from product) — link CONFLUENCE-1203\- Tech primer: private vs hosted tradeoffs — include charts for latency vs cost\- Case study (anonymized regional bank) — failures → lessons learned

Voice/Call script bullets (quick)\- Intro (30s): "Jordan Kim, partner lead at Redwood Inference — we help product + infra teams run LLMs at bank-grade risk levels."\- Pain probe (2–3 mins): "What forced this conversation? Speed, cost, compliance? Any recent incidents?"\- Value pitch (1–2 mins): "We give you a continuum — hosted, dedicated, private — with the same API and observability so you can start with hosted and move to private without rearchitecting."\- Close (15s): "Would you be open to a 30-min pilot kickoff? We'll bring SRE + compliance SME and a short checklist for your security review."

Obvious follow-ups to add to calendar after call\- Share pilot statement-of-work + data sharing checklist\- Intro between Priya and our compliance engineer (Aisha Patel)\- 30-min deep-dive on latency constraints with their Platform SRE

Short TODOs (personal)\- Draft 1-page tailored to Novus (deadline: Fri 2026-03-05) — include compliance matrix, pilot timeline + budget band\- Ask Marcus (solutions eng) for anonymized latency case study (JIRA: ENG-PILOT-332)\- Pull logs/metrics template for audit ingestion (CONFLUENCE-1203)

Random notes / brain dump\- If Novus prioritizes on-prem, emphasize our "private control plane" + KMS/HSM patterns. Show small POC we can drop into their environment w/o data egress.\- Consider offering an "SLA-backed performance pilot" with refund clause if we miss P95 targets during pilot window (good negotiation sweetener).\- Price cue: banks prefer commit-based reserved capacity for predictability; show 3-tier commit examples (small/med/large).

End of scratchpad — iterate into a proper one-pager after call notes land.
